A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LeAD-M3D. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection accuracy, runtime measurements and ablations on KITTI, Waymo and Rope3D, including extensive supplementary experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds cross-dataset generalization, augmentation, depth-error and inference-parameter analyses.

M1.justification: The A2D2, CM3D and CGI3D components remain. However, the stated depth objective changes the log-uncertainty coefficient from 1/2 in v1 appendix Eq. (12) to 1 in v2 appendix Eq. (11). This is a limited revision to the documented objective; whether implementation changed or the formula was corrected is unspecified.

E1.justification: v2 retains KITTI, Waymo and Rope3D and adds nuScenes front-camera training followed by KITTI evaluation, introducing actual cross-dataset generalization coverage. It also evaluates augmented KITTI validation images using RandAugment, CutMix and MixUp, expanding the tested input conditions.

E2.justification: The new domain-generalization comparison includes DGMono3D, MonoGDG, STMono3D and MonoCT (v2 Table 5). Existing KITTI comparisons add MonoA2 and IDEAL-M3D and remove DA3D from corresponding test and validation tables. This introduces a distinct comparator family and revises established comparison sets.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a cross-dataset training/evaluation design, nuScenes training for 24 epochs at 75% resolution, augmented-validation depth-error evaluation and a k=5–500 inference sweep. The reported KITTI top-k setting changes from 50 to 25. Existing Waymo protocols are retained; these additions should not be mistaken for reruns of all original experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds augmentation alternatives and difficulty analyses (Tables 8 and 10), top-k sensitivity (Table 17), domain-shift evaluation and a teacher reference against retained student-scaling results (Table 20). Conversely, v1's qualitative CM3D matching study in Appendix B.4 and Figure 6 is removed. Existing backbone, pretraining and detector-transfer ablations remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report median latency over 1000 forward passes and approximately ±0.2 AP variation associated with TensorRT. Neither adds training-seed aggregation, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new mean and median depth errors are evaluation metrics, not repeated-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: New results include nuScenes-to-KITTI AP of 45.50/32.14/28.56 (v2 Table 5), augmentation comparisons, depth errors, top-k results and teacher AP of 20.87. The no-clean-images ablation's Easy AP changes from 17.19 to 27.19, and N-model validation Moderate AP changes from 18.41 to 18.37 alongside the reported top-k revision. Most retained benchmark scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The appendix changes the mathematical depth-loss definition: the coefficient multiplying log sigma becomes 1 instead of 1/2. This is not equivalent notation. Other mathematical material largely elaborates existing detection losses and representations; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central three-component method, LiDAR-free detection and accuracy–runtime claims remain. v2 adds strong domain generalization to the introduction's contributions and conclusion, extending the claimed demonstrated applicability beyond v1's separate benchmark training and cross-view evaluation.

C2.justification: v2 interprets augmentation-induced depth errors as evidence for useful teacher–student asymmetry and discusses transferable representations and student capacity gaps. Its pretraining discussion replaces v1's assertion that MS-COCO initialization provides no inherent advantage with a more qualified acknowledgment of pretraining benefits. Open-vocabulary extensions are newly discussed.

D1.justification: v2 expands anchor and loss documentation, replaces abstract CGI3D pseudocode with PyTorch-style pseudocode, and discloses 34-hour teacher and up-to-60-hour student training times plus nuScenes settings. Exact dataset split counts given in v1 disappear. Most existing implementation details remain; the expanded pseudocode contains an undefined indices_k variable.

R1.justification: The original M3D, distillation and real-time detection positioning remains. v2 adds domain-generalization, augmentation and recent-detector literature, and Appendix A.2 explicitly distinguishes CGI3D from RoI-Align, proposal-refinement and query-based approaches. DA3D and the rotation-representation reference by Zhou et al. are removed.

P1.justification: The introduction, method explanations, experimental discussion and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. The appendix is reorganized into expanded architecture/training documentation, separately headed analyses and future work. Contribution bullets become continuous prose, and the original contents listing is removed.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, with extensively regrouped tables and relocated figures. KITTI and Rope3D qualitative figures gain zoomed details and revised color coding. The CM3D matching figure is replaced by different MixUp examples, and new analysis tables and additional table columns are introduced.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides direct cross-dataset evidence and targeted tests of augmentation asymmetry, depth accuracy and top-k selection (Tables 5, 6, 8, 10 and 17), strengthening empirical support. The gains are incremental to v1's already extensive evaluation. Unexplained loss-formula revisions, removed split counts and the undefined variable in Algorithm 1 limit the reproducibility benefits.
